views.name: bls_series_metadata
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  series_id,
  'employment_hours_earnings_series' AS source_table,
  supersector_code,
  industry_code,
  data_type_code,
  seasonal,
  series_title,
  footnote_codes,
  begin_year,
  begin_period,
  end_year,
  end_period
FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls.employment_hours_earnings_series`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  series_id,
  'unemployment_cps_series' AS source_table,
  NULL AS supersector_code,
  NULL AS industry_code,
  NULL AS data_type_code,
  seasonal,
  series_title,
  footnote_codes,
  begin_year,
  begin_period,
  end_year,
  end_period
FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls.unemployment_cps_series`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  series_id,
  'wm_series' AS source_table,
  NULL AS supersector_code,
  industry_code,
  datatype_code AS data_type_code,
  seasonal,
  series_title,
  footnote_codes,
  begin_year,
  begin_period,
  end_year,
  end_period
FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls.wm_series`
grain: one row per series_id per source_table (series metadata row)
views.description: Canonicalized union of series metadata tables (employment_hours_earnings_series, unemployment_cps_series, wm_series). Use to enrich time-series facts with series-level attributes like seasonal, industry codes, and series_title. Preserve series_id and key code columns for joins. | Use for: Join series metadata to facts to filter by industry/seasonal; list active series; identify series lifespan and attributes

views.name: cpsaat18_industry_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  sector,
  subsector,
  industry_group,
  industry,
  SUM(total_employed_in_thousands) AS total_employed_in_thousands,
  AVG(percent_women) AS avg_percent_women,
  AVG(percent_white) AS avg_percent_white,
  AVG(percent_black_or_african_american) AS avg_percent_black_or_african_american,
  AVG(percent_asian) AS avg_percent_asian,
  AVG(percent_hispanic_or_latino) AS avg_percent_hispanic_or_latino
FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls.cpsaat18`
GROUP BY year, sector, subsector, industry_group, industry
grain: one row per (year, sector, subsector, industry_group, industry)
views.description: Aggregated summary of employed population by industry from cpsaat18: total employed (thousands) and demographic percentages. Useful for comparisons across years or industry groups and for computing derived demographic counts. | Use for: Compare employment levels by industry/year; compute demographic counts by multiplying percentages by totals; trend analysis across years

views.name: qcew_2007_q3_industry_unpivoted
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  geoid,
  area_fips,
  'qtrly_estabs' AS metric_type,
  SPLIT(col, '_')[SAFE_OFFSET(2)] AS industry_code,
  CAST(val AS FLOAT64) AS metric_value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.2007_q3`,
UNNEST([
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_11_agriculture_forestry_fishing_and_hunting' AS col, qtrly_estabs_11_agriculture_forestry_fishing_and_hunting AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_1024_professional_and_business_services' AS col, qtrly_estabs_1024_professional_and_business_services AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_61_educational_services' AS col, qtrly_estabs_61_educational_services AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_53_real_estate_and_rental_and_leasing' AS col, qtrly_estabs_53_real_estate_and_rental_and_leasing AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_1023_financial_activities' AS col, qtrly_estabs_1023_financial_activities AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_31_33_manufacturing' AS col, qtrly_estabs_31_33_manufacturing AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_23_construction' AS col, qtrly_estabs_23_construction AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_1029_unclassified' AS col, qtrly_estabs_1029_unclassified AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_71_arts_entertainment_and_recreation' AS col, qtrly_estabs_71_arts_entertainment_and_recreation AS val),
  STRUCT('qtrly_estabs_1011_natural_resources_and_mining' AS col, qtrly_estabs_1011_natural_resources_and_mining AS val)
]) AS unpiv
WHERE val IS NOT NULL
grain: one row per (geoid, column unpivoted) representing a single metric for an industry
views.description: Unpivot selected industry columns from the wide QCEW 2007_q3 table into a tall format (industry_code, metric, value). Useful when analyses require comparing the same metric across industries or joining to county-level identifiers. This unpivots any qtrly_estabs_*, avg_wkly_wage_*, month3_emplvl_* columns into rows. | Use for: Compare establishments/employment/wages across industries within a county; join tall QCEW metrics to other geographic tables
